# Plan: `GLProgram.setI` and removal of the per-scene sampler-location copies (#349)

Pinned to commit 8a1fecb. Every line number below is from `git show 8a1fecb:<path>`. Re-grep before editing, because a checkout that is behind will differ. Nothing on screen may change. There is no speed goal.

Do not edit any file under `src/render/scenes/private/`. Nothing about paid scenes goes in this repo.

## 0. Facts I read (trust these)

- `src/render/gl.ts` has NO top-of-file header comment (line 1 is `export function createGL`). `GLProgram` (interface around line 73) has `program`, `use`, `setF`, `setV2`, `setV4`, `setFv`, `setV3v`, `setV4v` and `dispose`. `createProgram` builds a closure-private `locations` Map plus `loc(name)`. `loc(name)` caches `null` too (it checks `=== undefined`, not falsiness). The cache lives and dies with the returned object, so it dies with the program.
- A uniform call with a `null` location is a no-op in WebGL2, so passing `loc(name)` straight to `gl.uniform1i` behaves exactly like the scenes' old `gl.uniform1i(samplerLoc(...), unit)`.
- Eight scenes carry the same helper: `samplerLoc(gl, prog, key, name)` with a `samplerLocs: Map<string, WebGLUniformLocation | null>`, cleared with `samplerLocs.clear()` in `init` and `dispose`. They are:
  - `src/render/scenes/powder.ts` (map at ~1775, helper ~1799, clears ~1898 and ~2203)
  - `src/render/scenes/physarum.ts` (map ~939, helper ~956, clears ~1039 and ~1203)
  - `src/render/scenes/physarum2.ts` (map ~2329, helper ~2464, clears ~2804 and ~3207)
  - `src/render/scenes/crystal/index.ts` (map ~263, helper ~292, clears ~374 and ~509)
  - `src/render/scenes/shards/index.ts` (map ~237, helper ~247, clears ~345 and ~458)
  - `src/render/scenes/silk/index.ts` (map ~346, helper ~370, clears ~472 and ~595)
  - `src/render/scenes/slats/index.ts` (map ~194, helper ~208, clears ~298 and ~456)
  - `src/render/scenes/tessera/index.ts` (map ~334, helper ~357, clears ~444 and ~606)
- Call sites all have the shape `gl.uniform1i(samplerLoc(gl, <prog>, "<tag>.<name>", "<name>"), <unit>)`. The string key is a made-up cache key and is NOT the uniform name, so use the 4th argument (`name`) as the setter's name.
- physarum2 line ~2991 uses `` `${depKeyPrefix}uAgentPos` `` as the key, with a comment explaining that the two deposit programs have separate WebGLProgram objects. Per-program caching in `createProgram` makes that comment and the prefix unnecessary. Delete both, including the `depKeyPrefix` const (check with grep that nothing else uses it).
- `tests/powder.test.ts` (~lines 33-50) and `tests/sky.test.ts` (~lines 43-61) build `GLProgram` stubs with `as unknown as GLProgram`. They have no `setI`, and the cast hides that from the type checker. Only code that calls `setI` on those stubs needs it. Run the suite to see. If a test fails with "setI is not a function", add `setI: noop` to that stub.
- Other scenes use the same idea differently (tier B below). `tangle/index.ts` has `loc()` plus `sampler()` (~313-332), with its own `locs` Map<GLProgram, Map> cleared at ~451 and ~672. `gates/index.ts` has `intLoc()` (~718) plus `intLocs`, cleared at ~814 and ~1000.
- UNVERIFIED: whether every scene's `docs/scenes/<id>.md` exists for tier-B and tangle/gates scenes. I confirmed records exist for crystal, physarum, physarum2, powder, shards, silk, slats and tessera, and none of them mentions `samplerLoc`, `GLProgram` or "integer setter". Run `ls docs/scenes` before editing others.
- UNVERIFIED: that `npm run typecheck` includes `tests/`. Run the commands in section 6 and trust their output.

## 1. `src/render/gl.ts`

1. Add a top-of-file header comment (the file has none; CLAUDE.md says to explain the code at the top of its file). Keep it short and put no numbers or lists in it. Say that:
   - this file is the WebGL2 plumbing: context creation, loss handling, shader and program building, the fullscreen triangle, and canvas sizing;
   - `GLProgram` caches uniform locations per program object, so a rebuilt program starts with an empty cache and callers never clear anything;
   - samplers and other integer uniforms go through `setI` (for a sampler the value is the texture unit), and scenes must not keep their own location caches or call `gl.getUniformLocation` themselves.
   Do not list the setters by name or count them.
2. Add to the `GLProgram` interface, next to `setF`:
   ```ts
   /** Sets an integer uniform. For a sampler, `v` is the texture unit. */
   setI(name: string, v: number): void;
   ```
3. Add to the object `createProgram` returns, right after `setF`:
   ```ts
   setI: (name, v) => gl.uniform1i(loc(name), v),
   ```
   Do not wrap it in `if (l)`. `uniform1i(null, v)` is already a no-op, and the cached `null` already stops repeat lookups.
4. Pitfall: `setI` uploads to the program currently in use. Every site already calls `prog.use()` before setting uniforms, so keep each replacement exactly where the old `gl.uniform1i` was and do not move it.

## 2. Replace the eight `samplerLoc` copies (required)

For each of the eight files:
1. Delete the `const samplerLocs = new Map...` line.
2. Delete the whole `samplerLoc` function together with its doc comment. In powder.ts that comment says "GLProgram has no integer setter", and in shards/crystal/silk/slats/tessera there is an equivalent "idiom" comment. Delete them, because they are false now.
3. Delete every `samplerLocs.clear();` line, in both `init` and `dispose`.
4. Rewrite each call mechanically:
   `gl.uniform1i(samplerLoc(gl, X, "tag.uName", "uName"), N);` becomes `X.setI("uName", N);`
   Example: `gl.uniform1i(samplerLoc(gl, compositeProg, "comp.uSharpTex", "uSharpTex"), 0);` becomes `compositeProg.setI("uSharpTex", 0);`
5. If the removal leaves a local `gl` or an imported type (`GLProgram`) unused in that file, remove the unused item. Check with the type checker or lint (see section 6). Import `GLProgram` only if something still uses it.
6. physarum2 only: also delete the `depKeyPrefix` const and its 3-line comment. The two calls become `depositActive.setI("uAgentPos", 0);` and `depositActive.setI("uAgentDir", 1);`. Keep the `mrt` variable if anything else uses it.

Pitfall: do not use the string key as the uniform name. For example, the key `"pt.uVelZW"` has the uniform name `"uVelZW"`, and the unit for it in powder (3) must be preserved as written. Do not renumber units.

## 3. Also required, same pattern in two more scenes

- `src/render/scenes/gates/index.ts`: the `intLocs` Map, the `intLoc(gl, prog, tag, name)` helper and its two clears (~814, ~1000) go away. Calls at ~902-903, ~946 and ~962-964 become `gateProg.setI("uObjCount", n);`, `gateProg.setI("uCopies", copies);`, `blurProg.setI("uTex", 0);`, and `compProg.setI("uSharpTex", 0)`, `compProg.setI("uGlowATex", 1)`, `compProg.setI("uGlowBTex", 2)`.
- `src/render/scenes/tangle/index.ts`: its `sampler(gl, prog, name, unit, tex)` helper keeps the `activeTexture` and `bindTexture` calls but sets the unit with `prog.setI(name, unit);` instead of `loc` plus `uniform1i`. `loc()` and `locs` stay, because `uniformMatrix3fv(loc(...))` (uRot) and `uniform3f(loc(...))` (uGround) still need locations. Leave them unless you want to go further; do not widen the setters in this PR beyond `setI`.

## 4. Tier B (optional, do after the required parts are green; each is a small separate edit)

Hand-cached locations. For each, delete the `…Loc` variable, its assignment in `init`, its `= null` in `dispose`, and replace `gl.uniform1i(xLoc, N)` with `<prog>.setI("<uniform>", N)`:
- `fluid.ts`: dyeLoc "uDye" (0), edgeLoc "uEdge" (1), velSimLoc "uVelSim" (2), boltsLoc "uBolts" (3), all on `displayProg`. Declared ~1535-1545, assigned ~1558-1570, used ~1736-1770, nulled ~1794-1801.
- `sky/sky.ts`: dyeLoc "uDye" on `displayProg` (declared ~1730, assigned ~1790, used ~1952, nulled ~1968).
- `meshGrid.ts`: historyLoc "uHistory" on `meshProg` (~1335, 1403, 1572, 1653).
- `coil/index.ts`: scenePrevLoc "uPrevB" on `sceneProg`, blitFrameLoc "uFrame" on `blitProg` (~212-213, 290-291, 384, 398, 417-418).
- `petri.ts`: simPrevLoc, seedPrevLoc and displayPrevLoc, all "uPrev", on simProg, seedProg and displayProg (~729-731, 762-764, 936, 953, 984, 1008-1010).
- `toonrave/index.ts`: texLoc "uTex" on `post` (~334, 412, 564, 582).
- `storm.ts`: the per-call lookups at ~3254-3255 (`uNoise` 0, `uShape` 1 on `prog`) and ~3308-3309 (`uShape` 1, `uFlowTex` 2 on `filProg`).
- `ambience.ts` (formALoc, formBLoc and staggerLoc are plain int uniforms, not samplers, ~1180-1182 and ~1271-1273): `dotProg.setI("uFormA", choreo.formA())` and so on.
- SKIP: `chladni.ts`, `fluidSim.ts` (its `usesSplats` needs a raw `getUniformLocation` null test on an array uniform), `alien/*`, `compositor.ts`, `chaikin`, `coderain` and `pictureReadback.ts`. They mix raw locations with other uses, and the issue calls tier B optional. Mention in the PR description that they were left.

If tier B is done, treat it as part of the same PR but keep it in its own commit.

## 5. Docs and records (CLAUDE.md rules)

- Header comments: only gl.ts needs a new one (section 1). Check the headers of the scenes you touch, and fix any that mention a scene-local sampler helper (grep the changed files for "samplerLoc" and "integer setter" afterwards; both must return nothing under `src/`).
- Scene records: every touched scene must get an entry in the same PR. For each touched scene with a record at `docs/scenes/<id>.md`, add one line to "Decisions and pivots" (newest last), dated 2026-10-10, such as "Sampler units now set with `GLProgram.setI`; the scene's own location cache is gone; no visual change (#349)". Do not touch "Materials" or "References". Do not copy numbers from code. Records for these scenes were confirmed: crystal, physarum, physarum2, powder, shards, silk, slats, tessera.
- Do not add anything to docs for this (it spans no concept that needs a doc). Do not run `/exec-cheap`.

## 6. Tests

Create `tests/glProgram.test.ts` (vitest) with a fake `WebGL2RenderingContext` cast through `unknown`. The fake needs these members:
- `VERTEX_SHADER`, `FRAGMENT_SHADER`, `COMPILE_STATUS`, `LINK_STATUS` constants;
- `createShader`, `shaderSource`, `compileShader` and `deleteShader` (no-op or returning `{}`);
- `getShaderParameter` and `getProgramParameter` returning true;
- `createProgram` returning a fresh `{ id: n }` object each call;
- `attachShader`, `linkProgram`, `useProgram` and `deleteProgram`;
- `getUniformLocation(program, name)` that increments a counter, pushes `[program, name]` to a log, and returns a fresh unique object per call, except it returns `null` when `name` is `"uMissing"`;
- `uniform1i(loc, v)` that pushes `[loc, v]` to a log.

Tests, with non-trivial expected values:
1. Repeated sets share one lookup. Create one program. Call `setI("uTex", 3)`, then `setI("uTex", 7)`, then `setI("uOther", 5)`. Expect exactly 2 `getUniformLocation` calls (uTex and uOther), and a `uniform1i` log of three entries: (locTex, 3), (locTex, 7), (locOther, 5), with locTex strictly the same object in the first two and different from locOther. Must fail if: `setI` is not cached (3 lookups); `setI` uses `gl.uniform1f` (log empty); the argument order is swapped (values wrong).
2. Per-program cache. Create two programs from the same fake gl. Call `a.setI("uTex", 1)` and `b.setI("uTex", 2)`. Expect 2 lookups, with `[progA, "uTex"]` and `[progB, "uTex"]`, and two different location objects uploaded with values 1 and 2 in order. Must fail if the cache is a module-level or gl-level Map keyed by name only (the second call would reuse program A's location and upload to a wrong location, giving 1 lookup).
3. Inactive uniform: `p.setI("uMissing", 4)` three times. Expect exactly 1 lookup for `"uMissing"` and 3 `uniform1i` calls, each with location `null` and value 4. Must fail if the code caches only truthy locations (for example `if (!l)` or `l ?? lookup`), which would give 3 lookups.
4. Setter shares cache with the float setters: `p.setF("uTex2", 0.5)` (also needs `uniform1f` in the fake) followed by `p.setI("uTex2", 2)` gives 1 lookup total. Must fail if `setI` builds its own separate cache.

Because the fake's `createProgram` returns distinct objects per call, assert on the logged program objects, not on counters alone.

Also run the existing suite. `tests/powder.test.ts` and `tests/sky.test.ts` stubs may need `setI: noop` if their code reaches a `setI` call (UNVERIFIED).

Do not write a "scene still renders the same" unit test. The scenes need a real GL context. The visual check is in section 7.

## 7. Verification commands (run all; paste results in the PR)

1. `npm run typecheck` (must be clean; it will catch an unused import and a leftover `samplerLoc` call).
2. `npm test` (all tests, including the new `tests/glProgram.test.ts`).
3. Revert check for the new test: temporarily change `setI` to use `gl.uniform1f`, or drop caching, and confirm tests 1-3 fail; then restore.
4. `grep -rn "samplerLoc\|samplerLocs\|intLoc" src/` must return nothing (tier B aside, also `grep -n "Loc = gl.getUniformLocation" src/render/scenes` returns only the skipped files).
5. `npm run build` (confirms es2017 target and the type checks pass together).
6. Visual check: use the `/run` or `/pr-shots` flow (`npm run pr-shots`) to take headless screenshots of each touched scene before and after this change, on the same seed and time. For the 8 required scenes plus gates and tangle, the images should match within noise. Mention in the PR that no on-screen change is expected and what was compared. UNVERIFIED: the exact pr-shots arguments; read `tools/pr-shots.mjs`'s header first.
7. Finish with `/ship` (draft PR). The description should: say the cleanup removes the per-scene copies; list the scenes converted; list the skipped files from section 4; and carry the #335 coordination note from the overlap field. End the PR body with the attribution lines given in the session reminder.

## 8. Pitfalls summary

- Keep `.use()` before each `setI` (uniforms go to the bound program).
- Use the uniform name, not the cache key string, as `setI`'s first argument.
- Do not leave dangling comments claiming GLProgram has no integer setter; both the helper doc comments and the physarum2 `depKeyPrefix` comment must go.
- Do not add anything to `private/`.
- Do not copy counts or lists into comments (CLAUDE.md): the gl.ts header must not enumerate the setters.

- Version numbers: scenes' versions derive from git history (`tools/sceneVersionLib.mjs`), so there is nothing to bump by hand. Do not edit `sceneMajors.json`.

# Plan for #356: flash with Web Animations instead of a forced reflow

Do not edit anything under `src/render/scenes/private/`. This change touches no scene, so no scene record is needed.

## What the code does now (read at 8a1fecb, `src/ui/audioMeters.ts`)

Three places restart a fade by writing a "lit" inline style with `transition = "none"`, reading `offsetWidth` (a forced style and layout pass), then re-enabling the transition.

1. `blink(el, color)` (~l.743) is used only by the meter row's `flash(color)` (~l.907). The Section row calls it for the drop flash at ~l.2824: `section.flash(HOT_RED)`.
   - The fill has `transition: FADE`, where `FADE = "background-color 0.3s ease-out"` (~l.418).
   - `flash()` sets `flashed = true`.
   - The next `setValue()` writes `fill.style.backgroundColor = restColor`, which triggers the 0.3s ease.
   - `setFillColor()` skips the write while `flashed` is true.
   - `restColor` starts as `spec.accent`.
2. `flashRow(el)` (~l.759) is called by `revealRow` (~l.2862).
   - It sets an inline `box-shadow` ring and reads `offsetWidth`.
   - It sets `transition: box-shadow 0.6s ease-out`.
   - It clears `boxShadow` in a `requestAnimationFrame`.
   - It clears the transition in a `setTimeout` after `ROW_FLASH_MS` (900).
   - `.vc-row` in controlsTheme.ts has its own `transition: box-shadow 0.18s` and a hover ring, so the animation's end value must be "whatever the stylesheet says", not a fixed value.
3. `createTempoBlock(...).update(lock, beat)` (~l.953).
   - On a beat it sets `transition: none`, then `backgroundColor = "#fff"`, `boxShadow = 0 0 6px 1px ${BEAT_COLOR}` and `transform = scale(1.6)`.
   - It then reads `offsetWidth` and sets `transition = DOT_EASE`, then `lit = true`.
   - On the next frame `settle()` writes the rest values: `restColor`, `0 0 0 0 transparent`, `scale(1)`. That starts the 0.55s fade.
   - `DOT_EASE` is `"background-color 0.55s ease-out, box-shadow 0.55s ease-out, transform 0.55s ease-out"`. It is also in `tempoDotStyle` as `transition: ${DOT_EASE}`.
   - `restColor` is only written to the dot inside `settle()`. A lock change between beats is not shown until the next beat and its following frame.
   - `BEAT_COLOR = HOT_RED = "#ef4444"`.

## Design

Add a tiny shared helper, `src/ui/flashAnimation.ts`, and use it in all three places. Reasons:
- One place owns "cancel the previous flash on this element, start a new one".
- It is testable in the node test environment (see Tests).
- It removes the rAF/setTimeout/`transition` bookkeeping in `flashRow`.

Behaviour change to accept and note in the PR: the old dot held the lit look for about one frame before the fade began. The new one fades from the moment of the beat, roughly 16 ms earlier on a 550 ms fade. This is not worth emulating.

### 1. New file `src/ui/flashAnimation.ts`

Start the file with a header comment saying:
- What it is: a flash is a jump to a lit look that eases back to a resting look.
- Why it exists: it replaces the old "transition off, write the lit style, read `offsetWidth`, transition on" trick. Reading `offsetWidth` forces a style and layout pass in the middle of a frame. The Web Animations API needs none.
- Cancelling: a new flash on the same element cancels its previous one. That is why a per-element `WeakMap` is used.
- The animation does not fill, so after it ends the element shows its ordinary inline or stylesheet value. Callers must therefore keep that underlying value correct.
- Support: the helper no-ops where `Element.animate` is missing.
- Do not put numbers from the callers in the comment.

Code shape (TypeScript, es2017-safe):

```ts
/** The slice of Element a flash needs, so a test can hand in a stub. */
export interface Flashable {
  animate?: (keyframes: Keyframe[], options: KeyframeAnimationOptions) => { cancel(): void };
}

const running = new WeakMap<object, { cancel(): void }>();

/**
 * Jump `el` to `from`, then ease to `to`. Omit `to` to ease to whatever the
 * element's own style resolves to (a stylesheet value the caller can't name).
 */
export function flash(
  el: Flashable,
  from: Keyframe,
  to: Keyframe | null,
  durationMs: number,
  easing = "ease-out",
): boolean {
  running.get(el)?.cancel();
  running.delete(el);
  if (typeof el.animate !== "function") return false;
  const anim = el.animate(to ? [from, to] : [from], { duration: durationMs, easing });
  running.set(el, anim);
  return true;
}
```

Details:
- `WeakMap` and `Keyframe` are fine for es2017. Check that `Keyframe` and `KeyframeAnimationOptions` typecheck under the repo's TS lib; if not, use `Record<string, string | number>`.
- Cancel the previous animation BEFORE creating the new one.
- Use a plain `el.animate(...)` call, not `Reflect` or other tricks, so `this` is correct.
- `fill` is left at its default, `"none"`.

### 2. `src/ui/audioMeters.ts`

Add `import { flash as flashAnimate } from "./flashAnimation.ts";`. The name `flash` is already used as a method name there, so the alias avoids confusion.

**blink / meter row**
- Change `blink` to `blink(el, color, restColor)`:
  ```ts
  function blink(el: HTMLElement, color: string, restColor: string): void {
    flashAnimate(el, { backgroundColor: color }, { backgroundColor: restColor }, FADE_MS);
  }
  ```
- Replace `const FADE = "background-color 0.3s ease-out"` with `const FADE_MS = 300;` and `const FADE = \`background-color ${FADE_MS}ms ease-out\`;`. The fill's CSS transition stays so a `setFillColor` change still eases.
- In the row factory, `flash(color)` becomes `blink(fill, color, restColor);`.
- Remove the `flashed` variable and its three uses:
  - in `setValue`: delete the `if (flashed) { fill.style.backgroundColor = restColor; ... }` block;
  - in `flash`;
  - in `setFillColor`: always write `fill.style.backgroundColor = color` after updating `restColor`.
- The inline background now always equals `restColor`, so when the animation ends the fill is already correct. This is the central invariant. Update the comment on `restColor` and the doc comment on `flash()`; it currently says "fades back to the resting colour on the next setValue()".
- Pitfall: the animation's end keyframe is the `restColor` at the moment of the flash. If `setFillColor` changes it mid-fade, there is a small snap at the end. Only the Loudness row calls `setFillColor`, and it never flashes (UNVERIFIED: I saw `lufsRow.setFillColor` at ~l.2745 and `section.flash` at ~l.2824, but did not check whether any other row calls `.flash`). Run `grep -n "\.flash(" src/ui/audioMeters.ts` to confirm. Do not add handling for the snap.

**flashRow**
- Rewrite as:
  ```ts
  const ROW_FLASH_MS = 600;
  function flashRow(el: HTMLElement): void {
    flashAnimate(el, { boxShadow: "0 0 0 1px #fff, 0 0 16px 2px rgba(255,255,255,0.5)" }, null, ROW_FLASH_MS);
  }
  ```
  `to === null` gives a single-keyframe animation whose end is the element's underlying box-shadow. That is the stylesheet's resting or hover ring, which is what clearing the inline style used to land on.
- Delete the rAF, the `setTimeout` and the long coalescing comment, which no longer applies. Do not keep `ROW_FLASH_MS = 900`. The old 900 was a cleanup timer; the real fade is 0.6s. Rename the constant if that is clearer.
- UNVERIFIED: whether implicit "to" keyframes work in the oldest browsers this panel must support (they are in current Chrome, Firefox and Safari, from memory). If the target-browser check fails, use `{ boxShadow: "0 0 0 1px transparent" }` as the end keyframe (it matches `.vc-row`'s resting value, controlsTheme ~l.487), or leave `flashRow` unchanged. The issue says "if it stays simple", so leaving it as is would be acceptable, but say so in the PR.

**tempo dot (`createTempoBlock`)**
- Replace the `DOT_EASE` constant with `const DOT_FADE_MS = 550;`.
- Remove `transition: ${DOT_EASE};` from `tempoDotStyle`. Keep the rest of the style (6px dot, 0.25-alpha rest tint, `box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 transparent`).
- Delete `lit` and `settle()`.
- In `update()`, when the quantised `step` changes, also write `dot.style.backgroundColor = restColor;` next to the existing `digits.style.color` write. Initialise it once at construction: `dot.style.backgroundColor` is already in `tempoDotStyle`, which is fine.

- It also fixes the old quirk where the rest tint only followed the lock after a beat. Mention that in the PR.
- The beat branch becomes:
  ```ts

    flashAnimate(
      dot,
      { backgroundColor: "#fff", boxShadow: `0 0 6px 1px ${BEAT_COLOR}`, transform: "scale(1.6)" },
      { backgroundColor: restColor, boxShadow: "0 0 0 0 transparent", transform: "scale(1)" },
      DOT_FADE_MS,
    );
  }
  ```
- Update the doc comment on `update()`; it says "a lit dot eases back to it on the frame after its beat". It should now say the flash is a Web Animation that eases to the resting tint, and that the inline tint is always the resting one.
- Do not add a `transition` back to the dot. A CSS transition on `background-color` plus a WAAPI animation would fight when the lock step changes mid-fade.

**Comments and header**
- Update the `src/ui/audioMeters.ts` header only where it describes flash mechanics. In the header at ~l.162 the dot is described as "a beat dot whose resting tint follows beatClock's tempoLock", which stays true. Check `grep -n "offsetWidth\|reflow\|jump" src/ui/audioMeters.ts` after editing and fix every stale comment. This includes the `blink` doc ("then re-arm the fade so the next color write eases back") and the `Same jump-then-fade shape as blink()` comment on `flashRow`.
- Per CLAUDE.md, do not copy numbers from code into comments. Name `FADE_MS`, `DOT_FADE_MS` and so on instead.
- No docs/ page is needed; this does not span several files in a way that needs one.

### 3. Other `offsetWidth` uses

`src/ui/widgets/itemBoxes.ts:324` (a die-spin restart, `void rollBtn.offsetWidth`) and `src/ui/scenePicker.ts` / `tooltip.ts` are out of scope. They are click-only or must measure. Do not touch them.

## Tests (vitest, node environment, so no DOM and no jsdom: use stubs like `tests/canvasSizer.test.ts`)

Create `tests/flashAnimation.test.ts`. Use a stub made of `vi.fn()` spies that records calls in order into one shared `calls: string[]` array, e.g. `animate` pushes `"animate:" + label` and returns `{ cancel: () => calls.push("cancel:" + label) }`.

findings.summary: flashRow passes a one-keyframe list ([{offset: 0, boxShadow: ...}]). Implicit end keyframes only arrived in Chromium 84, Firefox 75 and Safari 13.1. The build target in vite.config.ts exists for webOS 5/6 and Tizen 2018-2020 (Chromium 56-79). On those engines animate() throws, flashAnim's catch returns null, and revealRow's 'you're looking at the right row' cue no longer shows at all, where the old code worked. Fix: when flashAnim returns null, fall back to a plain inline flash, e.g. set el.style.boxShadow to the lit ring and clear it in a setTimeout/rAF, letting .vc-row's own box-shadow transition fade it. Or give an explicit second keyframe of the .vc-row base ring ('0 0 0 1px transparent'), accepting a snap to the hover ring when the flash ends. Note the chosen behaviour in the flashRow comment.

The new tests guard only flashAnim itself; breaking prev?.cancel() or the try/catch makes them fail. Nothing checks the wiring in audioMeters.ts. You could put back a dot.offsetWidth read in update(), drop the cancel by passing null as prev, or end the dot's keyframes somewhere other than restColor, and every test would still pass. If it is cheap, pull the beat-dot keyframe construction into a small exported pure function, e.g. beatDotKeyframes(restColor), and assert that its last keyframe equals the resting tint for a given lock. Or say in the PR that the wiring was checked by eye and in a performance trace, as the issue asks.
